library(LaplacesDemon) # IAT
library(wrswoR) # faster weighted sample


# sourceCpp("src/functions.cpp")

library(stringr)
library(readxl)

# combination of final pdfs
averaging_pdfs <- F
averaging_data <- T
conflation <- F

if( is.null(core.data[[station_id]]) | station_id == 469 ) next()
    print(station_id)
    age.reso <- 2
    sim_nr <- 1
    dims <- 300
    null.ratio.check <- FALSE
    metro_hastings <- FALSE
    bias_corr <- FALSE
    mean_median_trafo <- FALSE
    IRD <- FALSE
    
    
    core.data[[station_id]]$sitename

    # consider case 
    giesecke_prespa <- F
    past_climate_module <- F
    iznik_iso <- F
    case_studies <- F
    
    
    source("src/mcmc_prepare.R")  
    source("src/mcmc_conduction.R")    
    source("src/mcmc_trimming_posterior_trafo.R")
    
#     source("src/mcmc_trimming_posterior_trafo_per_ages.R")
    
#     source("src/mcmc_case_studies.R")
#     source("src/mcmc_trimming.R")

# via interquantile range
# tann
set.seed(2022)
prior_tann_sample <- rnorm(10000,prior.recent$mean.tmp,prior.recent$sd.tmp)
tann_thresh <- quantile(prior_tann_sample,c(0.25,0.75))
# pann
set.seed(2022)
prior_pann_sample <- rgamma(10000,shape=shape,rate=rate)
pann_thresh <- quantile(prior_pann_sample,c(0.25,0.75))

if(multiple){
    shape1 <- 3 # 4; 20; 100; 10; 5
    shape2 <- 3 # 2; 100; 20; 5; 2
    set.seed(2022)
    beta_samples <- rbeta(10000,shape1,shape2)
    pollen_thresh <- 0.3
    pollen_thresh <- iso_thresh <- c(quantile(beta_samples,0.25),quantile(beta_samples,0.75))
    if(diff(range(age)) >= 150000) iso_thresh[1] <- 0.2 # for long core ioannina (194)
}else{
    shape1 <- 3
    shape2 <- 3
    # threshold
    set.seed(2022)
    beta_samples <- rbeta(10000,shape1,shape2)
    corr_thresh1 <- mean(beta_samples) - 0.1
    corr_thresh2 <- mean(beta_samples) + 0.1
    pollen_thresh <- c(corr_thresh1,corr_thresh2)
    pollen_thresh <- iso_thresh <- c(quantile(beta_samples,0.25),quantile(beta_samples,0.75))
}


# spectral
shape4 <- 3
shape5 <- 3
# threshold
set.seed(2022)
beta_samples <- rbeta(10000,shape4,shape5)
corr_thresh1 <- mean(beta_samples) - sd(beta_samples)
corr_thresh2 <- mean(beta_samples) + sd(beta_samples)
# spec_thresh <- c(0.2,corr_thresh2) #c(corr_thresh1,corr_thresh2)
spec_thresh <- c(quantile(beta_samples,0.25),quantile(beta_samples,0.75))


# human impact thresholds
iso_hi_thresh <- c(iso_thresh[1],1)
spec_hi_thresh <- c(spec_thresh[1],1)

iso_thresh <- c(0.2,1)
    spec_thresh <- c(0.2,1)
    spec_hi_thresh <- c(spec_hi_thresh[1],1)
    iso_hi_thresh <- c(0.05,1)
}else if(sitename == "En Gedi"){
#     pollen_thresh <- c(0.2,0.55)
#     iso_thresh <- c(0.2,1)
    spec_thresh <- c(spec_thresh[1],1)
    spec_hi_thresh <- c(spec_hi_thresh[1],1)
    iso_hi_thresh <- c(0.05,1)
}else if(sitename == "Lake Ohrid"){
    pollen_thresh <- c(pollen_thresh[1],1)
    iso_thresh <- c(iso_thresh[1],1)
    spec_thresh <- c(spec_thresh[1],1)
}

averaging_pdfs <- T
averaging_data <- F

mean_median_trafo <- FALSE
taxa_weights_case_studies <- list()
for(i in 1:length(posterior_case_studies)){
# i <- 2
    
    if(i == 2 & any(sitename == c("En Gedi","Lake Kinneret", "Birkat Ram")) ) pollen_thresh <- c(0.5,1) 
    
    if(sitename == "Lake Ohrid"){
        if(i == 1){
            case_studies <- T
            source("src/mcmc_prepare.R")
            i <- 1
        }
        if(i == 2){
            case_studies <- F
            source("src/mcmc_prepare.R")
            i <- 2
        }
        pollen_thresh <- c(pollen_thresh[1],1)
        iso_thresh <- c(iso_thresh[1],1)
        spec_thresh <- c(spec_thresh[1],1)
    }

    
    climate_check <- inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_tann,tann_thresh) & inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_pann,pann_thresh)
    climate_check_mh <- inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$tann_mh,tann_thresh_mh) & inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$pann_mh,pann_thresh_mh)
    climate_check_lgm <- inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$tann_lgm,tann_thresh_lgm) & inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$pann_lgm,pann_thresh_lgm)
    climate_check_past <- inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$tann_past,tann_thresh) & inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$pann_past,pann_thresh)
    climate_check <- climate_check  & climate_check_lgm
 
    variance_check <- inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_pollen,pollen_thresh) & inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_iso,iso_thresh) & inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_spec,spec_thresh)
    variance_check_hi <- inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_iso_hi,iso_hi_thresh) & inside.range(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_spec_hi,spec_hi_thresh) #
    if(length(variance_check_hi) == 0) variance_check_hi <- TRUE
    best_combs <- which(  climate_check & variance_check & variance_check_hi  )
#     best_combs <- which(  climate_check & variance_check )
    
#     if(sitename == "Birkat Ram" & i == 2) best_combs <- which(  variance_check )

    if(length(best_combs) == 0) stop()
    

    energy <- round(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_pollen[best_combs],5) # maybe i have to set set.seed during the MCMC
    if(all(unique(energy) == 0.5) | any(sitename == c("Dead Sea","")))  energy <- round(posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_iso[best_combs],5)
    dupl_id <- independent_samples <- which(!duplicated( energy ))
    factor <- 1
    energy_temp <- energy[dupl_id]

# pareto in terms of the explained variances
    pollen_pareto <- posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_pollen[independent_samples] 
    iso_pareto <- posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_iso[independent_samples] 
    iso_hi_pareto <- posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_iso_hi[independent_samples]
    spec_pareto <- posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_spec[independent_samples]
    spec_hi_pareto <- posterior_case_studies[[i]]$post_spec_hi[independent_samples]
    pareto_input <- data.frame(iso_pareto = iso_pareto, spec_pareto = spec_pareto, pollen_pareto=pollen_pareto)
    pareto_output <- psel(pareto_input, high(spec_pareto) * high(pollen_pareto) * high(iso_pareto), top_level=100)
    if(length(variance_check_hi) > 1 ){
        pareto_input <- data.frame(iso_pareto = iso_pareto,iso_hi_pareto=iso_hi_pareto, spec_pareto = spec_pareto,spec_hi_pareto=spec_hi_pareto, pollen_pareto=pollen_pareto)
        pareto_output <- psel(pareto_input, high(spec_pareto) * high(spec_hi_pareto) * high(pollen_pareto) * high(iso_pareto) * high(iso_hi_pareto), top_level=100)
    }
    pareto_id <- as.integer(rownames(pareto_output))
    if(length(pareto_id) > 10) pareto_id <- pareto_id[1:10]
    independent_samples <- independent_samples[pareto_id]

final_reconstruction <- function(energy=energy,post.which.combs=post.which.combs, taxa_weights =taxa_weights, gibbs = FALSE,age=age,all.avail=all.avail,all.avail.age=all.avail.age,rho.d.g.a=rho.d.g.a,tf.x1.current=tf.x1.current,tf.x2.current=tf.x2.current,ecdf_ref1=ecdf_ref1,ecdf_ref2=ecdf_ref2,x1range.bck=x1range.bck,x2range.bck=x2range.bck){
    
    # place holder for reference reconstructions
    if(length(ecdf_ref1) == 1){
        ecdf_ref1 <- ecdf_ref2 <- array(0, dim =c(nrow(rho.d.g.a), dims))
    }
    
    # create all accepted reconstructions
    count <- 0
    combs_unique <- which(!duplicated(energy))
    energy <- energy[combs_unique] /sum(energy[combs_unique], na.rm=T)
    energy_weight <- (energy - max(energy, na.rm=T))/(min(energy, na.rm=T)-max(energy, na.rm=T))
    
#     if( !is.null(nrow(taxa_weights)) ) taxa_weights <- taxa_weights[combs_unique,]
    if( nrow(post.which.combs) <= 1 ){
#         post.which.combs <- t(as.matrix(post.which.combs))
        averaging_data <- F
        averaging_pdfs <- T
    }
    
    corr_check <- array(NA, dim = c(length(combs_unique),5))
    all_tmp_mean <- all_pann_mean <- array(NA, dim = c( length(combs_unique),length(age) ) )

nrow_taxa_array_depth <- nrow(all.avail.temp)
    taxa_means_depth <- colMeans(all.avail.temp, na.rm=T)
    
    taxa_information_age <- c(t(all.avail.age.temp))
    ncol_taxa_array_age <- ncol(all.avail.age.temp)
    nrow_taxa_array_age <- nrow(all.avail.age.temp)
    taxa_means_age <- colMeans(all.avail.age.temp, na.rm=T)
    
    sample_size <- 25000
    for(i in combs_unique ){ 
        
        count <- count + 1
          
        # reconstructions
        if(gibbs){
            which.taxa.unique[count,] <- post.which.combs[i,]
            pollen_info_depth <- all.avail.temp[,which.taxa.unique[count,]] / rowSums(all.avail.temp[,which.taxa.unique[count,]], na.rm=T)
            pollen_info_age <- all.avail.age.temp[,which.taxa.unique[count,]] / rowSums(all.avail.age.temp[,which.taxa.unique[count,]], na.rm=T)
            
            # depth
            tmp.recon.depth <- pollen_info_depth %*% tf.x1.current[which.taxa.unique[count,],]
            pann.recon.depth <- pollen_info_depth %*% tf.x2.current[which.taxa.unique[count,],]
            # age
            tmp.recon.age <- pollen_info_age %*% tf.x1.current[which.taxa.unique[count,],]
            pann.recon.age <- pollen_info_age %*% tf.x2.current[which.taxa.unique[count,],]
            # mean
            reconst_mean <- pollen_info_age %*% tf_x12_mean_current[which.taxa.unique[count,],]
            all_tmp_mean[count,] <- reconst_mean[,1]
            all_pann_mean[count,] <- reconst_mean[,2]
        }else{
#             mean_factor_depth <- taxa_weights[i,]/taxa_means_depth
            taxa.spectrum.depth <- matrix(taxa_information_depth * taxa_weights[i,],ncol = ncol_taxa_array_depth,nrow=nrow_taxa_array_depth,byrow=T)
            taxa.spectrum.depth <- taxa.spectrum.depth / rowSums(taxa.spectrum.depth, na.rm=T)

#             mean_factor_age <- taxa_weights[i,]/taxa_means_age
            taxa.spectrum.age <- matrix(taxa_information_age * taxa_weights[i,],ncol = ncol_taxa_array_age,nrow=nrow_taxa_array_age,byrow=T)
            taxa.spectrum.age <- taxa.spectrum.age / rowSums(taxa.spectrum.age, na.rm=T)
        
            # depth
            tmp.recon.depth <- taxa.spectrum.depth %*% tf.x1.current
            pann.recon.depth <- taxa.spectrum.depth %*% tf.x2.current
            # age
            tmp.recon.age <- taxa.spectrum.age[reconst_ages,] %*% tf.x1.current
            pann.recon.age <- taxa.spectrum.age[reconst_ages,] %*% tf.x2.current
            if(taxa_change){
                tmp.recon.age2 <- taxa.spectrum.age[ages_lg,] %*% tf.x1.current_change
                pann.recon.age2 <- taxa.spectrum.age[ages_lg,] %*% tf.x2.current_change   
                tmp.recon.age <- rbind(tmp.recon.age,tmp.recon.age2)
                pann.recon.age <- rbind(pann.recon.age,pann.recon.age2)
            }
            # mean
            reconst_mean <- taxa.spectrum.age[reconst_ages,] %*% tf_x12_mean_current
            if(taxa_change){
                reconst_mean2 <- taxa.spectrum.age[ages_lg,] %*% tf_x12_mean_current_change
                reconst_mean <- rbind(reconst_mean,reconst_mean2)
            }
            all_tmp_mean[count,] <- reconst_mean[,1]
            all_pann_mean[count,] <- reconst_mean[,2]
        }

# conflation
        # depth
        tmp_mixt_confl_depth <- tmp_mixt_confl_depth * tmp.recon.depth
        tmp_mixt_confl_depth <- tmp_mixt_confl_depth / rowSums(tmp_mixt_confl_depth, na.rm=T)
        pann_mixt_confl_depth <- pann_mixt_confl_depth * pann.recon.depth 
        pann_mixt_confl_depth <- pann_mixt_confl_depth / rowSums(pann_mixt_confl_depth, na.rm=T)
        # age
        tmp_mixt_confl_age <- tmp_mixt_confl_age * tmp.recon.age
        tmp_mixt_confl_age <- tmp_mixt_confl_age / rowSums(tmp_mixt_confl_age, na.rm=T)
        pann_mixt_confl_age <- pann_mixt_confl_age * pann.recon.age 
        pann_mixt_confl_age <- pann_mixt_confl_age / rowSums(pann_mixt_confl_age, na.rm=T)
#         # emd
#         tann_ecdf <- cumsum(tmp_mixt_confl_age[1,])
#         pann_ecdf <- cumsum(pann_mixt_confl_age[1,])
#         emd1 <- (1/dims) * sum( abs(tann_ecdf - recent_tann_ecdf))   
#         emd2 <- (1/dims) * sum( abs(pann_ecdf - recent_precip_ecdf))
#         emd_confl[count] <- (emd1 + emd2)/2
        
    }
    
#     X11();plot(emd_avg_pdfs,ty="l",ylim = c(0,max(c(emd_avg_pdfs,emd_avg_data,emd_confl))) )
#     lines(emd_confl,col = "blue")
#     lines(emd_avg_data,col = "red")
    
#     means_emd <- c(mean(emd_avg_pdfs),mean(emd_avg_data),mean(emd_confl))
    
    pann_trafo <- spline( x2range.bck,seq(min(x2range.bck),max(x2range.bck),length.out=dims), n=1000 ) 
    # which combination technique
    if(averaging_pdfs){
        tmp.recon.depth.mixt <- tmp_mixt_avg_pdfs_depth
        pann.recon.depth.mixt <- pann_mixt_avg_pdfs_depth
        tmp.recon.age.mixt <- tmp_mixt_avg_pdfs_age
        pann.recon.age.mixt <- pann_mixt_avg_pdfs_age  
    }else if(averaging_data){
        tmp.recon.depth.mixt <- pann.recon.depth.mixt <- array(NA, dim =c(length(depth), dims))
        for(j in 1:length(depth)){
            tmp.recon.depth.mixt[j,] <- tmp_mixt_conv_depth[[j]]
            pann.recon.depth.mixt[j,] <- pann_mixt_conv_depth[[j]]
            # pann trafo
            pann_expand <- spline( pann_mixt_conv_depth[[j]], n=length(pann_trafo$x) )$y
            pann_interpol <- c()
            for(k in 1:length(pann_expand)){
                trafo_id <- which.min(abs(pann_trafo$x[k] - pann_trafo$y))
                pann_interpol[k] <- pann_expand[trafo_id]
            } 
            pann.recon.depth.mixt[j,] <- pann_interpol[seq(1,length(pann_interpol),length.out=dims)]
        } 
        tmp.recon.age.mixt <- pann.recon.age.mixt <- array(NA, dim =c(length(age), dims))
        for(j in 1:length(age)){
            if(anyNA(tmp_mixt_conv_age[[j]])) next()
            tmp.recon.age.mixt[j,] <- tmp_mixt_conv_age[[j]]
            pann.recon.age.mixt[j,] <- pann_mixt_conv_age[[j]] 
#             x2range.bck <- seq(min(x2range.bck),max(x2range.bck),length.out=dims)
            # pann trafo
            pann_expand <- spline( pann_mixt_conv_age[[j]], n=length(pann_trafo$x) )$y
            pann_interpol <- c()
            for(k in 1:length(pann_expand)){
                trafo_id <- which.min(abs(pann_trafo$x[k] - pann_trafo$y))
                pann_interpol[k] <- pann_expand[trafo_id]
            } 
            pann.recon.age.mixt[j,] <-  pann_interpol[seq(1,length(pann_interpol),length.out=dims)]
        }
    }else if(conflation){
        tmp.recon.depth.mixt <- tmp_mixt_confl_depth
        pann.recon.depth.mixt <-  pann_mixt_confl_depth  
        tmp.recon.age.mixt <- tmp_mixt_confl_age
        pann.recon.age.mixt <-  pann_mixt_confl_age   
    }
    
    
     
    
    # normalize mixture models to pdfs
    tmp.recon.depth.mixt <- tmp.recon.depth.mixt / rowSums(tmp.recon.depth.mixt, na.rm=T)
    pann.recon.depth.mixt <- pann.recon.depth.mixt / rowSums(pann.recon.depth.mixt, na.rm=T)
    
    tmp.recon.age.mixt <- tmp.recon.age.mixt / rowSums(tmp.recon.age.mixt, na.rm=T)
    pann.recon.age.mixt <- pann.recon.age.mixt / rowSums(pann.recon.age.mixt, na.rm=T)
    
      
    # mean of mixture models
    tmp.mixture.depth.mean <- pann.mixture.depth.mean <- tmp.mixture.depth.median <- pann.mixture.depth.median <- c()
    for(d in 1:ncol(rho.d.g.a)){
        tmp.mixture.depth.mean[d] <- weightedMean(x1range.bck,tmp.recon.depth.mixt[d,], na.rm=T)

# thinning
dims <- 300
which_samples <- seq(burn_in+1,sample_length, by=thin_size)
# which_samples <- seq(burn_in+1,sample_length, by=1)

energy <- round(posterior$post_pollen[which_samples],5) # maybe i have to set set.seed during the MCMC
if(all(unique(energy) == 0.5) | any(sitename == c("Dead Sea",""))) energy <- round(posterior$post_iso[which_samples],5)

dupl_id <- which(!duplicated( energy ))
which_samples <- which_samples[dupl_id]

# # trimming
# which_samples <- 1:sample_length
# climate_check <- inside.range(posterior$post_tann[which_samples],tann_thresh) & inside.range(posterior$post_pann[which_samples],pann_thresh)
# variance_check <- inside.range(posterior$post_pollen[which_samples],pollen_thresh) & inside.range(posterior$post_iso[which_samples],iso_thresh) #& inside.range(posterior$post_spec[which_samples],spec_thresh)
# which_samples <- which_samples[which( climate_check & variance_check )]
# dupl_id <- which(!duplicated( energy ))
# which_samples <- which_samples[dupl_id]

all.avail.age.temp <- taxa.spectrum.age <- all.avail.age
all.avail.depth.temp <- taxa.spectrum.depth <- all.avail
for(j in 1:num_taxa){
    all.avail.depth.temp[,j] <- all.avail[,j]/max(all.avail[,j], na.rm=T)
    all.avail.age.temp[,j] <- all.avail.age[,j]/max(all.avail.age[,j], na.rm=T)
}

taxa_information_age <- c(t(all.avail.age.temp))
ncol_taxa_array_age <- ncol(all.avail.age.temp)
nrow_taxa_array_age <- nrow(all.avail.age.temp)

taxa_information_depth <- c(t(all.avail.depth.temp))
ncol_taxa_array_depth <- ncol(all.avail.depth.temp)
nrow_taxa_array_depth <- nrow(all.avail.depth.temp)



ct1 <- ct2 <- 0
all_tmp_mean <- all_pann_mean <- array(NA, dim = c(length(which_samples),length(age)))
all_tmp_mean_depth <- all_pann_mean_depth <- array(NA, dim = c(length(which_samples),length(depth)))
for(i in which_samples){

    taxa.spectrum.depth <- matrix(taxa_information_depth * posterior$taxa_weights[[i]],ncol = ncol_taxa_array_depth,nrow=nrow_taxa_array_depth,byrow=T)
    taxa.spectrum.depth <- taxa.spectrum.depth / rowSums(taxa.spectrum.depth, na.rm=T)

    reconst_mean <- taxa.spectrum.depth %*% posterior$tf_sample[[i]]
    ct1 <- ct1 + 1
    all_tmp_mean_depth[ct1,] <- reconst_mean[,1]
    all_pann_mean_depth[ct1,] <- reconst_mean[,2]


    taxa.spectrum.age <- matrix(taxa_information_age * posterior$taxa_weights[[i]],ncol = ncol_taxa_array_age,nrow=nrow_taxa_array_age,byrow=T)
    taxa.spectrum.age <- taxa.spectrum.age / rowSums(taxa.spectrum.age, na.rm=T)

    reconst_mean <- taxa.spectrum.age %*% posterior$tf_sample[[i]]
    ct2 <- ct2 + 1
    all_tmp_mean[ct2,] <- reconst_mean[,1]
    all_pann_mean[ct2,] <- reconst_mean[,2]

}

# depth
post_tann_array_depth <- post_pann_array_depth <- array(NA, dim = c(length(depth), dims))
post_tann_quarts <- post_pann_quarts <- array(NA, dim = c(length(depth), 3))
for(i in 1:ncol(all_tmp_mean_depth)){
    # densities per time step
    post_tann_dens_temp <- density(all_tmp_mean_depth[,i],from=min(x1range.bck), to= max(x1range.bck), n = dims)
    post_tann_dens_temp$y <- post_tann_dens_temp$y/sum(post_tann_dens_temp$y)

# age
post_tann_array <- post_pann_array <- array(NA, dim = c(length(age), dims))
post_tann_quarts <- post_pann_quarts <- array(NA, dim = c(length(age), 3))
for(i in 1:ncol(all_tmp_mean)){
    # densities per time step
    post_tann_dens_temp <- density(all_tmp_mean[,i],from = min(x1range.bck), to= max(x1range.bck), n = dims)
    post_tann_dens_temp$y <- post_tann_dens_temp$y/sum(post_tann_dens_temp$y)
    
    post_pann_dens_temp <- density(all_pann_mean[,i],from = 0, to= 6000, n = dims)
    post_pann_dens_temp$y <- post_pann_dens_temp$y/sum(post_pann_dens_temp$y)
    
#     # quartiles
#     set.seed(2023)
#     post_tann_sample <- sample(post_tann_dens_temp$x,size=10000,prob = post_tann_dens_temp$y,replace = T)
#     set.seed(2023)
#     post_pann_sample <- sample(post_pann_dens_temp$x,size=10000,prob = post_pann_dens_temp$y,replace = T)
#     
#     post_tann_quarts[i,] <- quantile(post_tann_sample,c(0.25,0.5,0.75))
#     post_pann_quarts[i,] <- quantile(post_pann_sample,c(0.25,0.5,0.75))

    # posterior densities summary
    post_tann_array[i,] <- post_tann_dens_temp$y

So far, we have only examined the mean values of the reconstructions.
However, for a final climate reconstruction, we want to include the uncertainty information that results from the probabilistic transfer functions.
There are many ways to do this, and we will briefly introduce some of them below and finally present the most appropriate one for our concern.\par
% The following parts describe the final output, which includes the information from \acrshort{iat}.
As a first step, the chains in Fig. \ref{fig:prespa_trace} are first pruned by selecting those samples that lie within the interquartile ranges of the individual prior distributions.
In a second step, trimming is continued until the \acrshort{iat} is below 1.3.
Finally, a Pareto optimum is used to select the samples closest to the corresponding prior means.
Here the user can define how many samples are to be selected at the end.
Initial tests show that 10 individual reconstructions contain enough variability to describe large parts of the \acrshort{mcmc} simulation.
For this reason, 10 samples are always considered for each quantitative climate reconstruction in the following discussions.\par

The next method excludes the disadvantages mentioned above.
That is, it reduces the variances due to the additional information of independent reconstructions and has the same average mean as the input distributions \parencite{hill2008}.
A respective result is shown in Fig. \ref{fig:prespa_reconstruction} and is calculated via the mean of the input random variables:
$Z_N = \frac{\bm{\mathscr{C}}_1+\bm{\mathscr{C}}_2+...+\bm{\mathscr{C}}_N}{N} = \Tilde{\bm{\mathscr{C}}}_1+\Tilde{\bm{\mathscr{C}}}_2+...+\Tilde{\bm{\mathscr{C}}}_N$.
Here the constant $1/N^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}$ is chosen with $\alpha = 1$.
The latter is called the characteristic exponent of the stable density \parencite{honerkamp2002}.
As a result, $1/N$ compresses the limit distribution around a point.
This means that for larger values of $N$ a realization of $Z_N$ scatters less and less around the mean of $Z_N$ \parencite{honerkamp2002}, which explains the shape of the \acrshort{pdf}s in Fig. \ref{fig:prespa_reconstruction}.
To calculate them, we use the fact that the \acrshort{pdf} of the sum of the random variables can be obtained by calculating the convolution of the respective \acrshort{pdf}s (cf. Eq. \ref{eq:convolution}):
$\mathbb{P}_{Z_N}(\bm{C})= \mathbb{P}_{\Tilde{\bm{\mathscr{C}}}_1}(\bm{C}) \ast \mathbb{P}_{\Tilde{\bm{\mathscr{C}}}_2}(\bm{C}) \ast ... \ast \mathbb{P}_{\Tilde{\bm{\mathscr{C}}}_N}(\bm{C})$.
% More precisely, the \acrshort{pdf} of the sum of random variables can be obtained by calculating the convolution (cf. Eq. \ref{eq:convolution}) of the corresponding \acrshort{pdf}s \parencite{honerkamp2002}:
% $\mathbb{P}_{Z_N}(\bm{C})= \mathbb{P}_{\Tilde{\bm{\mathscr{C}}}_1}(\bm{C}) \ast \mathbb{P}_{\Tilde{\bm{\mathscr{C}}}_2}(\bm{C}) \ast ... \ast \mathbb{P}_{\Tilde{\bm{\mathscr{C}}}_N}(\bm{C})$.
Although more time consuming to compute, all subsequent local climate reconstructions are based on this combination method because it has exactly the advantageous properties we want for such reconstructions.\par
At first glance, it can be seen that the course of the annual temperature in Fig. \ref{fig:prespa_reconstruction} (a) is similar to the reference curves in Fig. \ref{fig:prespa_reference}.
